concepts.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
concepts.gloss: Θ, Ω and o express tight, lower and strictly-smaller asymptotic bounds on functions, alongside the upper bound O.

concepts.name: Logarithms and exponentials
concepts.gloss: The logarithm is the inverse of exponentiation, with log_2 counting bits and the natural log based on e, and logs of products being sums of logs.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling
concepts.gloss: The floor and ceiling of a real number are the greatest integer not above it and the least integer not below it.

concepts.name: Limits and liminf
concepts.gloss: The limit of a sequence is the value its terms approach, and the limit inferior is the smallest value its terms keep returning near.

concepts.name: Geometric series
concepts.gloss: A sum of terms with a fixed ratio r<1 (or growing with ratio r>1) is bounded by a constant times its largest term.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.gloss: A proof that a statement holds for all natural numbers by proving a base case and that each case implies the next.

concepts.name: Recurrences and divide-and-conquer analysis
concepts.gloss: The running time of a recursive algorithm satisfies an equation in terms of its cost on smaller inputs, solved by unrolling the recursion tree or by the master theorem.

concepts.name: Worst-case running time
concepts.gloss: The maximum number of steps an algorithm or machine takes over all inputs of a given size.

concepts.name: Lower bounds for computational problems
concepts.gloss: A lower bound states that every algorithm in a given model needs at least a certain amount of time on some inputs of each size.

concepts.name: Deterministic algorithm
concepts.gloss: An algorithm or machine whose next step is uniquely determined by its current state and input, with no randomness or nondeterminism.

concepts.name: Binary and radix representation
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a sequence of digits in base q, each digit weighted by a power of q, with base 2 giving bits.

concepts.name: Schoolbook addition and multiplication with carries
concepts.gloss: Integers are added digit by digit propagating carries, and multiplied by summing shifted partial products in quadratic time.

concepts.name: Karatsuba multiplication
concepts.gloss: A divide-and-conquer algorithm that multiplies two n-digit numbers with three half-size products instead of four, giving O(n^{log_2 3}) time.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The recursive radix-two algorithm that evaluates a length-2^k discrete Fourier transform in O(n log n) arithmetic operations, used in algorithms courses to multiply polynomials by evaluation at roots of unity and interpolation.

concepts.name: Two's complement and signed integer representation
concepts.gloss: Signed integers are stored either as a sign bit with a magnitude or in two's complement, where a k-bit pattern represents its value modulo 2^k in a range centered on zero.

concepts.name: Fixed-point binary fractions
concepts.gloss: Real numbers are approximated by integer multiples of 2^{-p}, with rounding or truncation producing an error at most 2^{-p}.

concepts.name: Bitwise XOR
concepts.gloss: The bitwise exclusive-or of two bit strings, which is addition modulo two in each position and is its own inverse.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers modulo q, in which a number is invertible (a unit) exactly when it is coprime to q.

concepts.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
concepts.gloss: The gcd of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, and the integers are coprime when it equals one.

concepts.name: Prime numbers
concepts.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than one with no divisors other than one and itself, and small primes can be found by trial division.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli s_1,…,s_d, residues modulo the product correspond bijectively, and compatibly with addition and multiplication, to tuples of residues modulo each s_i.

concepts.name: Integer division and integer square root
concepts.gloss: For integers a≥0 and b>0, division gives the unique q and r with a=bq+r and 0≤r<b, and the integer square root is the largest integer whose square is at most a.

concepts.name: Newton's method
concepts.gloss: An iterative root-finding method that refines an approximation by following the tangent line, roughly doubling the number of correct digits per step.

concepts.name: Sets, Cartesian products and cardinality
concepts.gloss: Basic set operations, including the Cartesian product of sets as the set of tuples and the size of a finite set.

concepts.name: Subsets and binomial coefficients
concepts.gloss: The k-element subsets of an n-element set, counted by the binomial coefficient n choose k.

concepts.name: Indicator vector
concepts.gloss: The 0/1 vector of a subset of a ground set, with a one in each coordinate that belongs to the subset, so that dot products count intersections.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijection of a finite set onto itself; permutations compose and have inverses.

concepts.name: Lexicographic order
concepts.gloss: Tuples are ordered by comparing their first coordinates, then their second on ties, and so on, as in row-major storage of arrays.

concepts.name: Sorting and stable radix sort
concepts.gloss: Sorting arranges records by key; a stable sort keeps the order of equal keys, which lets radix sort process one digit at a time.

concepts.name: Binary counters and amortized analysis
concepts.gloss: Incrementing a binary counter L times costs O(L) total bit changes because bit j flips only about L/2^j times.

concepts.name: Stack
concepts.gloss: A last-in first-out data structure, used to hold suspended work during depth-first recursion.

concepts.name: Directed graphs and acyclic networks
concepts.gloss: A directed graph has vertices joined by directed edges, and an acyclic one has no directed cycles, so it can model a circuit from sources to sinks.

concepts.name: Boolean and arithmetic circuits
concepts.gloss: A circuit is an acyclic network of gates computing functions of its inputs along wires, with size equal to its number of gates.

concepts.name: Matrix inverse, transpose and identity
concepts.gloss: The identity matrix leaves vectors unchanged, an invertible matrix has an inverse undoing it, and the transpose swaps rows and columns.

concepts.name: Special matrices
concepts.gloss: Diagonal, lower and upper triangular, permutation and all-ones matrices, whose shapes make products and inverses easy to compute.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues
concepts.gloss: An eigenvalue of a square matrix is a scalar λ with Ax=λx for some nonzero vector x, and the matrix is invertible exactly when 0 is not an eigenvalue.

concepts.name: Sup norm and the triangle inequality
concepts.gloss: The sup norm of a vector is the largest absolute value of its entries, and it satisfies the triangle inequality ‖a+b‖ ≤ ‖a‖+‖b‖.

concepts.name: Number systems and their notation
concepts.gloss: The standard symbols ℤ, ℚ, ℝ and ℂ for the integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers, with their arithmetic.

concepts.name: Fields and rings
concepts.gloss: A ring is a set with addition and multiplication obeying the usual laws, and a field is a ring in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.

concepts.name: Gaussian function
concepts.gloss: The function e^{-a x^2}, a smooth bell-shaped curve that decays rapidly away from zero.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: algorithms and data structures (asymptotic analysis, recurrences and divide-and-conquer, sorting including stable radix sort, amortized counting, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, and the textbook FFT for polynomial multiplication), theory of computation (Turing machines, tapes, deterministic machines, Boolean circuits, worst-case time and lower bounds), and discrete mathematics (sets, permutations, subsets and counting, induction, graphs, modular arithmetic, gcd, primes and the Chinese remainder theorem). From the supporting mathematics they have first-year calculus (limits, logarithms and exponentials, geometric series, Newton's method), introductory linear algebra (matrices, inverses, transposes, triangular and permutation matrices, eigenvalues, dot products and orthonormal bases) and complex numbers, plus the machine-level number representations of computer organization (binary and radix digits, two's complement, bitwise XOR, carries). They have not studied the research literature on fast integer multiplication, Gaussian resampling, synthetic polynomial transforms, multilinear algebra beyond the basics, bilinear-form theory, analytic number theory, or index coding.
